title: First professional job with Monroe Richardson's band at Midway Gardens
summary: A friend, later his brother-in-law, recommends him to a nine-piece band; they play weekends opposite Art Kassel at Midway Gardens.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I see. Well, did you start playing professionally when you were in high school?
Yes.
Tell me about that.
Well, there's one reason why I didn't finish school. A friend of mine heard me on tuba, and he recommended me to a band leader that had a orchestra.
Who was the friend? Was he a musician?
Yeah, he turned out to be -- later years he turned out to be my brother-in-law, name of Jimmy MacEndry. (PHONETIC).
I see.
He was the drummer in the band.
In the professional band?
In the professional band. So I started playing with them when I was in high school, and in the meantime.
What was the name of the band, do you recall?
The name of the band was -- what was his name? Henderson
Hennessey?
No, Henderson.
Henderson. Like Fletcher Henderson?
Yeah, like Fletcher, but -- Monroe Henderson. No, it wasn't Monroe, either. It was -- Monroe Richardson.
Richardson was the name of the band?
The name of the band.
How big a band was it?
It was about nine pieces.
Was -- would we have called it a jazz band, now?

Yes. See, back in those days they had what they called jazz bands, Creole jazz bands. And then they had white bands that played in ballrooms. We was playing opposite the white bands in Midway Gardens.
I see.
It's 60th and Cottage Grove.
When was this?
That was about 1925.
1925. You would have been 17?
Yeah.
About 17.
Just about.
Was it a regular gig, you know?
Yeah, well, on weekends. Like Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.
Uh-huh. And you played for dancing?
Yeah. And the band we played opposite was named Art Castle.
Oh, yeah. Yeah, that's a well-known band.
Yeah.
Where was Midway Gardens?
60th and Cottage Grove. Midway, there.
Do you recall who else was in the band that you were playing with?
Not offhand.
Uh-huh. How long did you play with that band?
I played with that band, oh, I guess it was about two or three months.
And you were still going to school?
